stack_arguments.observed_use: Nonzero enables the conditional clear path

order: Test byte[query+0x10] bit 0x04; if set, call the global function pointer with (1, query, 0, 0, 0, 0).
Test the stack byte; if nonzero and byte[query+0x10] bit 0x02 is clear, clear query+0x12 and query+0x10 as words.

callback.contract: void __cdecl(std::uint32_t, OpaquePreferenceQuery *, std::uint32_t, std::uint32_t, std::uint32_t, std::uint32_t)
callback.call_order: The callback runs before the conditional clear.

mechanics.null_paths: No null guard is added for query or the global callback pointer.

representative_callers.use: Preference query clear with an explicit zero stack byte

evidence.observation: The callback is conditional on flag bit 0x04 and clearing is conditional on the stack byte and absence of bit 0x02.
The exact six-word callback call uses stack cleanup 0x18, then the two flag words are conditionally zeroed.
The indirect global resolves to 0x009415a0 as the only direct callee.
The global callback slot is read by this target and adjacent property helpers.

unresolved_questions: What concrete service or property owner is installed at 0x0154eb48?
What do the two flag bits mean beyond their observed callback and clear behavior?
Which callers depend on callback timing or mutation of the query words?
blockers: The global callback owner and payload semantics are unresolved.
